subject.title: Generalize post-timeout compaction completion reconciliation across session state

question: Should OpenClaw promote the existing narrow compaction-count repair into a single compaction-completion reconciliation boundary, and which fields or plugin/context-engine signals should that boundary own?
rationale: The remaining work crosses session storage, `/status`, token freshness, and plugin/context-engine API contracts, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent owner boundary.

options.title: Keep as design tracker
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the reconciliation owner boundary and decide which session fields and plugin signals it owns.

options.title: Split into narrow trackers
options.body: Move the concrete plugin-engine count and post-compaction token/status work into narrower canonical issues before closing or narrowing this umbrella.

options.title: Limit to current counter fix
options.body: Declare the broader convergence model out of scope and rely on separate issue-specific repairs for each state mismatch.

recommendation.title: Keep as design tracker
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the reconciliation owner boundary and decide which session fields and plugin signals it owns.

likelyOwner.reason: jalehman has both context-engine feature history and direct review/co-author provenance on the narrow predecessor fix.
